message:
unknown, they don't need to protect themselves from the people who keep their accounts paid up to date or even pay forward a bit (as I do), yet they still do this.  Their concern is not for service to either their customers (us) OR the inmates, it is for their profits.  That is more than apparent if you either deal with them yourself or read even just this one blog with it's 144 responses let alone any of the other blogs on T-Netix/Evercom/Securus and Correctional Billing Services.

As far as pre-paying, plenty of people have been ripped off by doing that, posts on this thread discuss it.  People prepay but the money disappears or takes forever to make it into the inmates account, and then you have to deal with the constantly disconnected and dropped calls and the charges for each call connection when the inmate calls back (if he's lucky enough to be able to do that).

Sorry, I don't buy the just protecting their interests unless you mean protecting interests = make big profits by ripping people off.  As for HELPING ME BUDGET, I don't need THEIR help in budgeting my money, thank you very much.  Who are they to decide how much I can spend on phone calls in a 90 day period?!  Nobody should have that right as long as I am paid up and pay my bills on time!

Poor T-Netix/Evercom/Securus/CBS....here they are just looking out for us, helping us with our budgets and protecting themselves from us crafty phone bill dodgers.... uh, right.

As for pre-pay, there's no way I'm going to invest in a pre-pay account when so often others have and the money never makes it to the inmates account or the phone charges are jacked way up or the calls are constantly dropped and lines blocked anyway.  It's bad enough to endure all this crap while paying for it as-you-go, to give them a big hunk of money up front is just asking for trouble unless you don't mind throwing your money away, or burning it.
